Subject: Private deployment - sudden 503 spikes and request for immediate help

Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp degradation on our private deployment (PRIV-482) around 08:45 PDT this morning. Frontend is reporting increased request queue depth and intermittent 503s across our inference route. Client-side 95th p90 latencies jumped from ~180ms to >1.2s and error rates around 10-12% over the past 30 minutes. This is impacting our triage workflows.

Attached are a few snippets: sierra-kvcache-stats-20260503.csv and a gzipped chunk of the request logs (prod-logs-20260503.gz). We also see a lot of connection resets to the model workers.

We need:
- an immediate triage call (can you join now?)
- a short-term mitigation to reduce errors (routing to hosted fallback or temporary scale up)
- an ETA for a root cause and timeline to resolution — leadership is on the line.

Simon is on this thread and on standby.

— Alejandra
Director, Platform Reliability
Sierra Health

Subject: RE: Private deployment - sudden 503 spikes and request for immediate help

We're on the bridge and have pulled several metrics. Summary so far: 
- Observed sustained queue depth increase on the request router starting 08:43 PDT; backlog rose from ~40 to ~650 requests in 6 minutes.
- Autoscaler didn't trigger additional workers because the signal was coming from a custom metric (router.queue_unacked) that had a tags mismatch after a config push last night — threshold not evaluated for a subset of tenant routes.
- KV cache hit rate dropped to ~22% (cold start) which increased per-request model time; we also saw repeated worker OOMs on older runtime instances (runtime v1.7.9).
- 503s correlate with worker restarts and queue overflow.

Immediate remediation steps underway:
1) Bumped backlog_limit on the router for Sierra tenant to 1500 (temporary).
2) Manually spun up 6 prewarmed workers pinned to runtime v1.8.2; moving serving traffic to those instances now.
3) Patch ready for the autoscaler tag mismatch (small config change) — will redeploy canary in ~30m.
4) Enabling a temporary traffic split to Redwood hosted for 20% of traffic for the two critical endpoints (pending Alejandra confirmation).

I attached the trimmed logs we collected and the quick grep outputs showing worker exit codes. Will post more analysis after the canary.

— Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec summary: Sierra Health private deployment incident (impact, remediation, ask)

David / Rishi — quick exec summary to align on next steps and any credit/contract asks. Please let me know if you want to loop anyone else.

Impact: ~3 hours of elevated error rate (peak 12%) and increased latency for several customer-critical routes; customer reports partial service disruption to triage workflows. No data exfiltration or compliance breach identified.

Root cause (short): mis-tagged autoscaler metric combined with runtime v1.7.9 instance OOMs led to delayed scale-up and worker churn; KV cache cold starts magnified request latency. Full RCA pending.

Action taken: backlog_limit bumped, six prewarmed v1.8.2 workers provisioned, autoscaler tag fix deployed canary, temporary 20% routing to hosted fallback, OOM watchdog hotfix queued.

Ask / recommended customer compensation: offer a one-time service credit equivalent to 10% of May committed spend and a complimentary two-week capacity buffer on Dedicated pool while we complete the post-mortem. Grace will own the MOP and post-mortem.

Next steps & timeline:
- 24 hours: confirm host fallback stability and no recurrence (NA window).
- 72 hours: complete RCA, publish post-mortem, and deliver final remediation checklist.
- 7 days: verify workload stability, close MOP.

I'll be available to brief execs on the customer call tomorrow morning if needed.

— Marissa
